title: Main Landing Gear Bay Wiring — Brake Control and Wheel Speed Runs

ata.title: Centre Fuselage Wiring — Landing Gear Bay Wiring

abstract: Wiring diagram for the left main landing gear bay, covering the brake control unit interface, the wheel speed runs down the gear leg and the gear door proximity feeds.

sections.purpose: This sheet gives the wiring of the left main landing gear bay from the centre fuselage disconnect to the brake control unit and down the gear leg to the axle.
sections.sheet_note: The sheet shows the left bay; the right bay is on the companion sheet and is not symmetrically identical because the disconnect bracket is one frame further aft. The wheel speed runs down the gear leg are the highest maintenance item on the sheet: they move with the gear on every cycle and the loop clamp positions given here are what keeps the service loop away from the shock strut. A wheel speed run refitted with the loop the wrong way round will chafe within a few hundred cycles.
sections.routing_note: The bay feeds enter at the centre fuselage disconnect, run outboard along the bay roof and split at the brake control unit rack. The wheel speed runs continue down the leg in the protected conduit with a service loop at the shock strut, and the gear door proximity feeds branch at the bay sidewall.

ata.title: Centre Fuselage Wiring — Landing Gear Bay Wiring

abstract: Wiring diagram for the left main landing gear bay, covering the brake control unit interface, the wheel speed runs down the gear leg and the gear door proximity feeds.

sections.purpose: This sheet gives the wiring of the left main landing gear bay from the centre fuselage disconnect to the brake control unit and down the gear leg to the axle.
sections.sheet_note: The sheet shows the left bay; the right bay is on the companion sheet and is not symmetrically identical because the disconnect bracket is one frame further aft. The wheel speed runs down the gear leg are the highest maintenance item on the sheet: they move with the gear on every cycle and the loop clamp positions given here are what keeps the service loop away from the shock strut. A wheel speed run refitted with the loop the wrong way round will chafe within a few hundred cycles. Configuration note: the connectors at the brake control unit rack carry the reporting path to the maintenance system, and their identifiers are shown on this sheet and nowhere else in the wiring set. They are correct for every standard in service today. They are called out here because this sheet is the first document a line technician opens when a reported fault and the installed configuration disagree, so any change to what the control unit reports makes the mismatch visible here before it is visible anywhere else. The sheet is therefore held inside the documentation package of the retained-context candidate rather than assessed as unaffected by it.
sections.routing_note: The bay feeds enter at the centre fuselage disconnect, run outboard along the bay roof and split at the brake control unit rack, where the reporting path to the maintenance system leaves on the upper connector. The wheel speed runs continue down the leg in the protected conduit with a service loop at the shock strut, and the gear door proximity feeds branch at the bay sidewall. No route on this sheet changes with the candidate; only the identification of the reporting path connector is affected, and that identification is given above.
